answer: A river delta survey crew plants one willow pole per agent in the tidal mud as a tide staff, and each epoch the surveyor sets one real pearl into the pole at the measured high water line, carving the date beside it. A copied pole fails because the mud level, the carved date, and the pearl depth never match the crew log, and a pole moved or replanted loses its season. A thousand fake names need a thousand willow poles driven into real mud and a thousand pearls set at true high water marks.
